newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Six-month renewal for U.N. force on Golan Heights.
newsitem.headline: Six-month renewal for U.N. force on Golan Heights.

text.p: The Security Council on Wednesday unanimously approved a six-month renewal, until May 31, 1997, of the 1,040-member U.N. Disengagement Observer Force which has served as a buffer between the Syrian and Israeli armies on the Golan Heights since 1974.
The force, commanded by Major-General Johannes Kosters of the Netherlands, includes troops from Austria, Canada, Japan and Poland.
The Golan Heights, captured by Israel from Syria in the 1967 Arab-Israeli war, are the focus of long-stalled peace talks between the two countries.
UNDOF was established to monitor a ceasefire and troop separation agreement that followed the 1973 Middle East war, when the Golan Heights were again the scene of heavy fighting.
